q3_question_legal_status_presented.answer: YES — in the output-tool schema enum (['open', 'in_progress', 'answered', 'unresolved', 'blocked', 'deferred', 'superseded']); the frozen instructions never enumerate them; the projection shows only each question's CURRENT status value

q4_status_disposition_mapping_presented.answer: NO explicit mapping is presented anywhere in the model-visible input; instructions only say 'Dispositions, statuses and closure semantics remain your responsibility and are validated strictly'; the policy-layer rules (answered requires basis refs, unresolved requires basis+limitations+summary, blocked requires blocker) are NOT in the model-visible input
q4_status_disposition_mapping_presented.basis_rule_visibility: only the explicit-empty-list rule ('basis_handles: [] means no basis and will be rejected wherever basis is required') hints that some closures need basis

q5_confusion_prone_phrasing.assessment: the D* fresh-result envelope ('status': 'completed') is the single strongest confusion surface: the model is closing a question ABOUT a completed delegation and the input names both with the same field name 'status'. 'completed' reaches the model ONLY through that embedded envelope (never in the rules prose; the prose 'complete' hit is 'Never emit a complete working state', an unrelated prohibition). This is an input-level COLLISION FACT; whether it caused the model's choice is NOT provable from one sample

q6_schema_sufficiency.answer: the schema DOES express the distinction (per-kind enums in each action branch; to_status is enum-typed per branch), but the non-discriminated union means a wrong branch guess cascades; the schema presents the legal VALUES yet nothing in the input contrasts the run/delegation lifecycle vocabulary with the question vocabulary

causality_statement: HYPOTHESIS ONLY: the input collision plausibly primed the value choice, but one sample cannot establish causation; the schema presented the legal values and the model still chose an illegal one
